# Nose-Touch Avoidance Is Conserved Across *C. elegans* and Relatives

Nose touch avoidance behavior is conserved in five of the six species tested (Figure 5A). In *C. tripartitum*, animals showed an overall avoidance rate of less than 10% after the first few positive trials, which suggests this species adapts to the nose-touch stimulus faster than *C. elegans* and the others (Figure 5A). During the first three trials, however, *C. tripartitum* responded in a quantitatively similar way to *C. elegans* (Figure S2 in Additional file 2).

Ablation of the ASH neurons in five nose-touch responsive species abolished nose-touch avoidance (Figure 5A). Four of the five species still showed some nose-touch responses in 20–30% of trials (Figure 5A). *Caenorhabditis* sp. 3 was the exception; its ASH-ablated animals completely lost the ability to respond to nose touch (Figure 5A).

Ablation of the AWC neuron, by contrast, did not affect the response to nose touch in any of the species (Figure S3 in Additional file 2).

UPO-06: PrhI Gene Synthesis
UPO-06 carries the coding sequence for prhI from *Ralstonia solanacearum*. PrhI is an ECF sigma factor required for transcription driven by the Prh signal transduction system. PrhR activates the gene, which then controls sigma factor expression through activation of the PprhJ promoter. The sequence is optimized for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

UPO-11: PprhJ Promoter Synthesis
UPO-11 contains the PprhJ promoter region. The promoter responds to plant cell contact through signal transduction mediated by PrhA and PrhR, and it is activated by the ECF sigma factor PrhI. The sequence is optimized for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

In Fig. 15 the alitrunk is conspicuously swollen and sits much higher than the propodeal dorsum. The propodeum carries a pair of strong spines, straight to slightly upcurved. There is no metanotal groove, and the metapleural lobes are triangular and conspicuous. In profile the petiole has an elongate peduncle and a well-developed node whose dorsum slopes down posteriorly, leaving a short posterior face. On the postpetiole the anterior and dorsal surfaces form a single convexity, and the posterior face is truncated. In dorsal view the nodes of both petiole and postpetiole are broader than long.

The dorsum of the head is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5–7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye level. The rugae are irregular and meander slightly, usually with a few anastomoses. The scrobal area is largely smooth but usually has 1–2 fine rugulae crossing its width just behind the antennal fossa. Behind the eyes the sides of the head are finely reticulate-rugose, and this sculpture runs around the posterior margins of the scrobe to the occiput. The spaces between rugae are unsculptured, or at most show faint superficial traces.

The dorsal alitrunk is everywhere finely but strongly reticulate-rugose, with broad shining interspaces. The petiole dorsum is rugulose, while the postpetiole ranges from rugulose to only faintly sculptured. The gaster is unsculptured. All dorsal surfaces of the head and body are densely clothed with fine, acute hairs. The color ranges from dark reddish brown to blackish brown.

Subject: foxl2 Expression Patterns in Trout

Dear Customer,

Here is a summary of our findings on foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both foxl2 transcripts are expressed very early in development (Figure 2). foxl2a expression was highly restricted in the male, while the diverged paralog foxl2b was present in most adult extragonadal tissues examined (see Additional file 2).

In females, foxl2b expression was highly restricted in adult tissues, essentially confined to the skin, gill, and ovary. We also found foxl2b expression in the testis to be very strong, which fits with previous findings showing foxl2b present alongside the absence of foxl2a in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

Taken together, these results suggest that foxl2b may act as a critical regulator of male-specific genes (such as cyp19b1), particularly later in development.

Thank you for your interest in our research.

Best regards,

[Your Name]

Starting from the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975), we derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation and obtained the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Using only the linear dispersion relation for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). The leading-order solution shows that the modified curvature terms of the MMSE matter, while the slope square terms stay negligible, as the mild-slope assumption requires. So we kept all the modified curvature terms that the MSE drops, and this gave us a uniform model.

We then built a numerical model with the finite element method (FEM) to predict wave scattering by a varying bottom. The uniform model captures the main features of waves over various sea beds, including sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. For sinusoidal beds, its results agree more closely with experimental data than other established models. For man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model agree more closely with experimental data than the results of Kirby (1986).

The FEM model also applies to the transformation of waves over arbitrarily-varying bathymetry.

The myth of the Phaedrus is described with greater intensity than any that came before it, though it belongs to a different category. It deals with a former existence rather than a future one, and portrays a deep conflict between reason, supported by passion or righteous indignation, and the animal instincts within us. In that earlier life, the human soul traveled in the company of some god and saw truth in the form of the universal before birth, and our present existence is the outcome of a struggle that took place before it. This world is a relative thing, often projected into the future, much as we wonder where men were before their birth or what awaits them after death. The question "Where were men before birth?" feels unfamiliar and unnatural to us, yet it carries as much force and reach as the other. In the Phaedrus, the "spiritual combat" of this life is only a figure of speech. The majesty and power of the whole passage, especially the proem beginning "The mind through all her being is immortal," can only be rendered poorly in another language.

Welcome to the wild world of MapleStory. There are thousands of monsters roaming the world, so here is a quick breakdown of where they live and how to survive.

The weak monsters are the most common foes, found by towns. They wander aimlessly even if you bump into them, so don't worry. Just take the damage they deal.

The dangerous ones live deep in dungeons.

The aggro mechanic matters. Monsters usually roam aimlessly, even if you bump into them. But if you attack an enemy or cast a debuff on it, you aggro it. That means you get its attention and it will try to attack you back.

The behavioral pattern: most enemies attack by trying to run into you over and over again.

The best strategy against these persistent attackers is to attack them repeatedly. Your attacks usually have enough knockback to keep them in place.

Sometimes you will need to jump over them to dodge their attacks entirely. These are your dodge tactics.

For the full details, check out the complete list at MapleStory/Monsters/Complete list.

Remember: aggro is a two-way street. Stay safe and keep attacking.

We want to tell you something about early hearing development. Humans typically develop spoken language within the first few years of life. If a child cannot hear well, this can prevent them from learning to speak and also from understanding spoken language.

Often, the first sign that a severely hearing-impaired (deaf) child has a hearing deficit comes after communication problems have already caused issues within the family and hindered social skills. If the child grows up in a Deaf community where sign language is used instead of spoken language, these problems are much smaller (please see our article on Deaf Culture).

In many developed countries, babies get a hearing evaluation during the newborn period. The purpose is to prevent a deaf child from being isolated within a hearing family without anyone realizing it. Sign language is a full means of communication, but literacy ultimately depends on understanding speech. In most written language, the sound of the word is coded in symbols.

Someone who hears well enough to learn to speak and read will keep that ability to read even if their hearing later becomes too impaired to hear voices. Someone who never heard well enough to learn to speak is rarely able to read proficiently (see [4]). Most evidence suggests that identifying hearing impairment early is what allows a child with very insensitive hearing to learn spoken language effectively. Listening also matters when learning a second language.

We hope this makes the case for early intervention clear. If you have questions, please write to us.

Warm regards,

Transduction is how physical and chemical signals get converted into neural impulses. In the nervous system, it's the basic process of turning stimuli into electrical signals. In sensory transduction, specialized sensory receptors take physical or chemical inputs and turn them into electrical impulses that travel to the brain.

The visual system shows how this works. In the retina, rod and cone cells connect the physical environment to neural communication. When light strikes these photoreceptors, it changes the shape of the protein rhodopsin. That change starts a chain of events that alters the photoreceptor's electrochemical gradient. As the gradient drops, the electrical signals sent to the brain decrease. In other words, more light hitting the photoreceptor means fewer electrical impulses, and the brain uses that inverse relationship to make sense of what you see.

Few insects are as well known as the Glow-worm, a small creature that lights a lantern at its tail-end. People know its name even if few have seen it in the grass, glowing like a spark fallen from the full moon. The Greeks called it the Bright-tailed; modern science calls it *Lampyris*. Fabre's *Book of Insects*, though, was written for children. Its texts come from Alexander Teixeira de Mattos's unabridged translations of the *Entomological Memoirs*, which Mrs. Rodolph Stawell, author of *Fairies I Have Met* among other books, retold for young readers. Her versions are abridged and heavily revised, sometimes to the point of cutting things out entirely.

Subject: Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), often just called the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is made up of many former industrial cities, including Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

About five million people live here, so the region is considerably bigger than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. There are plenty of motorways, but hitchhiking can be hard because of the tangled network of minor roads. The main motorways are the A1, A2, and A3.

If you plan to hitch here, stay on these main motorways. The smaller roads are hard to work with because there is very little transit traffic. Germany is generally a good country for hitchhiking, but the Ruhr Area is by far the worst part of it for this. Hitching inside the Ruhr is a bit like hitching in a big city such as Istanbul; the cities are independent, but to a traveler they all feel like districts of one huge city.

We hope this helps you plan your trip.

Best regards,

Subject: Study Results: Lung Tissue Volume and Aeration Analysis

Dear Customer,

Here are the main findings from our analysis of lung tissue volume and functional changes.

The total volume of lung tissue was calculated as: volume of lung tissue = number of voxels × volume of the voxel, provided the compartment considered has a CT number above zero.

The change in functional residual capacity caused by PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) was computed as the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between the PEEP and ZEEP states. Alveolar derecruitment was defined as the difference in gas volume within poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions between these same conditions.

We also computed the changes in gas volume from PEEP withdrawal in normally aerated lung regions, defined by CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

As previously described in reference [21], the distribution of lost lung aeration for each patient (lung morphology) was classified as diffuse, patchy, or lobar based on the distribution of CT attenuations at ZEEP.

Mobile Gaming: The Next Step in Co-Creation

Mobile internet is changing what storytelling can do by putting electronic games on portable, location-aware interfaces. This is the latest step in a decades-long evolution of electronic games that try to make the player a co-author alongside the original designers, rather than just an avatar in a gameworld.

Location-aware interfaces let players pull places from the physical world into their gameworld, and the reverse, something no earlier interactive media allowed. Beyond giving players a hand in worldmaking, mobile games drop linear narratives in favor of cooperative storytelling built on the player's experience of place.

This "author-player" worldmaking idea is not new. Mobile games, however, push the process past the limits of traditional video games. By extending worldmaking beyond the screen into the physical world, location-aware interfaces use the player's sensory experience of real places as storytelling tools.

In our essay, we theorize the storytelling potential unique to mobile games and describe our experience trying to use that potential through the design and implementation of our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.
